extracted.intended_audience: users of the Magma computer algebra system; mathematicians and programmers working with enumerative combinatorics, incidence structures and graph theory
extracted.subtask_description: Reference/documentation for Magma functions and conventions for enumerative combinatorics (subsets, partitions, Bell numbers) and finite incidence structures and graphs, including constructors, returned objects, and semantics of testing/transforming structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsets vs PowerSet behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The function Subsets(S) should be distinguished from PowerSet(S). Both return the power set of S mathematically, but Subsets returns the subsets explicitly, whereas PowerSet merely returns them as a formal object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example output shows enumerated subsets. Use Subsets when you need an explicit enumerated set of subsets; use PowerSet when the formal object is sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: k-subset definition and Subsets(S, k)
rubrics_metrics.description: A k-subset of S is a subset of S having cardinality k (an unordered set of size k with distinct elements). Subsets(S, k) returns all k-subsets of S as an enumerated set of enumerated sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If k > n (n = |S|) then an empty set will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multisets, Subsequences, Permutations semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Multisets(S, k) returns all multisets of size k (counting multiplicity) with elements in S. Subsequences(S, k) returns all sequences (ordered multisets) of length k with elements in S. Permutations(S, k) returns all distinct-element sequences (ordered sets) of length k with elements in S. Permutations(S) is special for k = |S|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions allow ordered or repeated elements as appropriate; if k > n then an empty set is returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting formulae for subset-like objects
rubrics_metrics.description: If only the totals are needed, use the counting functions: number of k-subsets = Binomial(n,k); number of k-multisets = Binomial(n + k − 1, k); number of k-sequences = n^k; number of k-permutations = NumberOfPermutations(n,k) (or Factorial(n) if k = n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use counting functions from Table 35.1 when enumeration is unnecessary or expensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partitions(n) and partition ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: A partition of an integer n is a representation as the sum of positive integers, ignoring order. Partitions(n) returns a sequence containing all partitions of n, each partition given as a non-increasing sequence of positive integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NumberOfPartitions(n) returns the count; RestrictedPartitions(n, T) restricts component values to set T of positive integers (useful for coin-change style problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedPartitions semantics and example
rubrics_metrics.description: RestrictedPartitions(n, T) returns only those partitions whose components all lie in set T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: RestrictedPartitions(50, {5,10,20}) lists ways to give change for 50 cents using coins {5,10,20}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell numbers (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bell number B_n is the number of partitions of a set of n objects into non-empty subsets (with B_0 = 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple formulae and implementations are provided: via Stirling numbers, recursive summation, infinite series approximation, and generating functions; these have differing efficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell via Stirling numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: B_n = sum_{k=1..n} StirlingSecond(n,k) for n >= 1, with B_0 = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement by constructing StirlingSecond(n,k) sequence then summing (demonstrated Magma implementation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell via recursive summation (inefficiency warning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recursive formula: B_0 = 1; for n >= 1, B_n = sum_{k=0..n-1} Binomial(n-1,k) * B_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct recursive implementation is inefficient because intermediate B_k are recomputed repeatedly. Prefer computing and storing all B_k up to N as a recursively-defined sequence (memoization/sequence technique). Take care with Magma's 1-based sequence indexing when handling B_0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell via infinite series (numerical approximation)
rubrics_metrics.description: B_n = (1/e) * sum_{k=0..infty} k^n / k! .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PositiveSum for summation of positive terms; set real precision appropriately (e.g., precision depends on n). Numerical precision limits applicability to moderately small n; numerical analysis recommended to choose precision for larger n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bell via exponential generating function
rubrics_metrics.description: Exponential generating function: sum_{n>=0} B_n t^n / n! = exp(exp(t)-1). Coefficient extraction yields B_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use power series ring with sufficient precision and extract coefficient*Factorial(n); demonstrated Magma code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magma sequence indexing caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: Magma’s sequences are indexed beginning at 1, so special handling is required for terms corresponding to index 0 (e.g., B_0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations using sequences must adjust indices or treat B_0 separately to avoid off-by-one errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence structures: multi-sorted nature and returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidence structures are multi-sorted algebras with more than one carrier set (e.g., point-set and block-set). Every function/constructor returning an incidence structure also returns the point-set and block-set (or vertex-set and edge-set) as second and third return values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assigning an incidence structure to an identifier, users may assign the carrier sets simultaneously: I, P, B := incstr constructor. Many access operations for I involve P or B as the parents of basic objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blocks vs enumerated sets
rubrics_metrics.description: A block may be regarded as a set of points and limited set-style operations are supported for blocks, but a block is distinguished from a mere enumerated set of points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Set(block-set) / Set(line-set) to obtain ordinary sets of points for display or set-operations; be aware that blocks belong to special categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: IncidenceMatrix semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: IncidenceMatrix(I) returns the incidence matrix m of I as an integer matrix with #P rows and #B columns; entry m_ij = 1 iff point i is incident with block j, else 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IncidenceMatrix to inspect incidence relation numerically; can construct an incidence structure from an incidence matrix via IncidenceGraph or appropriate constructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality vs isomorphism for incidence structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Two incidence structures I and J in same category are equal if their point-sets and block-sets are equal (I eq J). An isomorphism maps P_I to P_J and B_I to B_J preserving incidence. IsIsomorphic(I,J) returns true and the isomorphism mapping if isomorphic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isomorphism testing has parameter AutomorphismGroups with values "None","Left","Right", or "Both" to specify which automorphism groups, if any, to construct first; changing this can speed some tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: AutomorphismGroup(I) return values and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: AutomorphismGroup(I) returns: the automorphism group G as a permutation group on a natural support Ω={1..n}, a G-set for the action on points, a G-set for blocks, the parent M for automorphisms represented as maps, and a transfer map t from G to M.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no repeated blocks support is P else P ∪ B. Use G-sets to compute orbits, stabilizers etc. Use t(g) or g@t to convert a permutation g ∈ G to the corresponding mapping on the incidence structure. Aut(I) returns M and t without constructing G.

rubrics_metrics.name: Block/Edge/LineGroup convenience
rubrics_metrics.description: BlockGroup(I), EdgeGroup(I) or LineGroup(I) return the automorphism group of I acting on the blocks (edges, lines) as a permutation group on the set of blocks, and the G-set of blocks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these when emphasis is on block-action rather than point-action (convenient alternative to AutomorphismGroup).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automorphism subgroup helpers for large structures
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing the full automorphism group G is too expensive, Magma offers functions computing useful subgroups: AutomorphismGroupStabilizer(I, k) computes subgroup fixing first k base points; AutomorphismSubgroup(I) computes a subgroup generated by one element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These functions return five values: the subgroup and the four auxiliary values as returned by AutomorphismGroup(I). They are helpful to test non-triviality of G without full computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simple graph definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A graph consists of vertices joined by edges. Simple graphs have no multiple edges between the same pair of vertices and no loops. Undirected graphs have no direction on edges; digraphs have directed edges. Here 'graph' denotes undirected simple graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Magma supports constructing both simple graphs and digraphs (digraphs not discussed in this chapter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph construction syntaxes
rubrics_metrics.description:
Standard graph constructors (CompleteGraph, BipartiteGraph, EmptyGraph, KCubeGraph, PathGraph, PolygonGraph, RandomGraph, RandomTree, MultipartiteGraph) provide common graphs. General constructor: Graph

.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Edge specification may be a list of sets of vertex pairs or a sequence of p sets giving neighbours of each vertex. Methods may be mixed; Magma combines information. In neighbour-sequence method it is permissible to specify adjacency only in one direction (asymmetric listing), Magma will infer edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: VertexSet/EdgeSet and Vertices/Edges semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: VertexSet(G) and EdgeSet(G) return sets in special categories VertSet and EdgeSet. Vertices(G) and Edges(G) return enumerated sets whose universes are those special sets. Universe(Vs) and Universe(Es) show the parent vertex-/edge-set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to ith vertex via G.i or V!i. Edge between u and v is E!{u,v} or E!{i,j}. Number of vertices Order(G) or #V; number of edges Size(G) or #E. Use ParentGraph to revert from subset to parent graph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph addition/subtraction semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Add/remove edges or vertices: G + {u,v} adds edge; G - e removes edge; G - v removes vertex (causes renumbering and removes incident edges). G - {u, v} removes vertices u and v (not an edge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful to distinguish using a set of two vertices (vertex removal) from using an edge object (edge removal): G - {u,v} vs G - E!{u,v}.

rubrics_metrics.name: sub< G | vertices > and sub< G | edges > constructors
rubrics_metrics.description: sub< G | list of vertices > constructs the subgraph induced by listed vertices (renumbered as needed); sub< G | list of edges > constructs subgraph with all vertices but only listed edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists may contain vertex/edge sets as well as individual vertices/edges. Coercion functions relate subgraph vertices/edges back to main graph via VertexSet(G) ! sub.i and EdgeSet(G) ! edge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotient graph construction (quo< G | partition >)
rubrics_metrics.description: quo< G | {P1,...,Pr} > constructs quotient graph by identifying vertices according to partition subsets Pi. Vertices of Q correspond to the Pi, and two vertices of Q are adjacent if some vertex in one subset is adjacent to some vertex in the other subset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Function Contract(S) also constructs graphs formed by identifying vertices in set S; Contract(u,v) and Contract(e) are special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard graph transformations (Complement, Contract, InsertVertex, LineGraph, Switch)
rubrics_metrics.description: Table of standard related graphs: Complement(G) (edges are exactly the non-adjacent pairs in G); Contract(u,v)/Contract(e)/Contract(S) identify vertices; InsertVertex(e)/InsertVertex(T) insert degree-2 vertices into edges; LineGraph(G) returns line graph; Switch(u)/Switch(S) toggle adjacency for neighbours of u or all vertices in S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these constructors for common graph manipulations; semantics described in table (see examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph unions and products semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: Union(G,H) gives graph with vertex-set V_G ∪ V_H and edge-set E_G ∪ E_H (treats vertices as disjoint); EdgeUnion(G,H) when G and H have same order identifies corresponding vertices; CompleteUnion(G,H) = Union(G,H) plus all cross-edges; LexProduct, CartesianProduct, TensorProduct, and G^n defined with vertex-set V_G × V_H and adjacency determined as per definitions (various product rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Union of two copies of same graph yields twice as many vertices; choose product appropriate to combinatorial construction needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph property test functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functions to test graph properties include IsBipartite(G), IsComplete(G), IsPath(G), IsPolygon(G), IsTree(G), IsForest(G), IsEmpty(G), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Semantics: IsTree(G) true if connected and has no cycles; IsForest(G) true if no cycles; IsEmpty(G) true if G has no edges; use these to assert/verify structural properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incidence, adjacency, and distance matrices for graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: IncidenceMatrix(G) is p×q with columns representing edges containing exactly two 1s at end-vertices. AdjacencyMatrix(G) is p×p with 1s for adjacent pairs. DistanceMatrix(G) is p×p symmetric with integer entries giving distances or -1 where not connected (as per Magma conventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use IncidenceGraph(M) to construct graph from incidence matrix. These matrices are useful for numeric computations and constructing other objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance, paths, connectedness and related functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Distance(u,v) returns length of shortest path or -1 if not connected. Geodesic(u,v) returns a shortest path (sequence) or empty sequence if not connected. Ball(u,n) returns set of vertices at distance ≤ n; Sphere(u,n) at distance exactly n. Diameter(G) returns length of longest path or -1 if not connected; DiameterPath returns a sequence realizing diameter. IsConnected(G), Component(u), Components(G) give connectivity information. Girth(G) and GirthCycle(G) give length and witness cycle respectively. IsEulerian(G) true if there is a cycle visiting each vertex exactly once (all vertices even degree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these functions for routing, distance-based queries, and cycle analysis; note -1 conventions for disconnected pairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cliques, independent sets and extremal functions
rubrics_metrics.description: CliqueNumber(G) returns maximum clique size; IndependenceNumber(G) returns maximum independent set size. LargestClique(G) and LargestIndependent(G) return example sets. Clique(G, n) returns a clique of cardinality at least n (empty if n > clique number); Independent(G, n) analogous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to analyze dense/sparse substructures and for reductions to combinatorial optimization problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chromatic number and index semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ChromaticNumber(G) returns minimum number of vertex colours so no adjacent vertices share colour. ChromaticIndex(G) returns minimum number of edge colours so no adjacent edges share colour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: KCubeGraph(3) has ChromaticNumber 2 and ChromaticIndex 3; consider maximum degree lower bounds and use these functions to compute exact colourings.

rubrics_metrics.name: AutomorphismGroup(G) for graphs
rubrics_metrics.description: AutomorphismGroup(G) returns the automorphism group of G (permutation group acting on vertices) and can be used to inspect order, generators, and action. The ^ operator computes action of an automorphism on a vertex (v ^ g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group actions can be applied to vertices, sets, or sequences via ^. Large multipartite graphs can have very large automorphism groups; CompositionFactors and other group functions can be applied to the returned group.
